boundary_note: Saragossa, frozen span 1808-12-19 to 1809-02-20. Replacement boundaries unset; phases are research hypotheses. This draft admits no features, changes no frozen winner and allocates no tactical or campaign credit.

claims.value: Bodart: side A (French) 42,000 infantry, 3,500 cavalry and 4,500 artillery/engineers, total 50,000; side B (Spanish) 30,000 garrison, mostly irregulars.
claims.rationale: Available-for-engagement figures under Bodart’s rounded-up convention (shared research-conventions index), unless the entry specifies a surrender population. Not an opening muster; components are not added twice. English rendering of the claim-relevant portion (ours): "side A (French) 42,000 infantry, 3,500 cavalry and 4,500 artillery/engineers, total 50,000; side B (Spanish) 30,000 garrison, mostly irregulars."

citations.locator: Bodart (1908), p. 393, Saragossa entry; page image inspected
citations.quote: Die Franzosen (42.000 Inft., 3.500 Kav., 4.500 Art. und Genie, 50 schwere Geschütze zus. 50.000 M.) unter Marschall Lannes nötigen die spanische Besatzung (30.000 M. mit 150 Kan.) (zumeist Irreguläre) unter Gen.-Kpt. Don José de Palafox nach beispiellos hartnäckiger Verteidigung (23tägiger Häuserkampf) zur Kapitulation, wonach der Rest der Garnison (noch 8.000 Dienstfähige) in Kriegsgefangenschaft geriet. Die Franzosen erbeuteten 145 Kan., 21 Fahn.

claims.value: Toreno gives side B an initially expected 14,000–15,000 defenders, rising to 28,000 with fugitives from Tudela; cavalry is separately described at 1,400.
claims.rationale: Stages and components are not added together. A provisioning capacity elsewhere on the page is not a troop return. English rendering (ours): "Initially only 14,000 or 15,000 were expected for defence; they increased to 28,000 with dispersed Tudela troops joining the garrison. Cavalry comprised 1,400 under Butrón."

citations.quote: En un principio no se contaba para la defensa sino con 14 ó 15,000 hombres: aumentáronse hasta 28,000 con los dispersos de Tudela que se incorporaron á la guarnicion.

claims.value: Toreno gives side A 35,000 in the third and fifth corps combined, excluding six artillery, eight sapper and three miner companies.
claims.rationale: Initial combined corps estimate, not whole-siege cumulative employment and not a French own return. Company headcounts remain unknown. English rendering (ours): "Their combined forces reached 35,000, excluding six artillery, eight sapper and three miner companies added to them."

citations.locator: toreno-t2, printed p. 266, Internet Archive leaf 271; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: ascendiendo sus fuerzas reunidas á 35,000 hombres, sin contar con seis compañías de artillería, ocho de zapadores y tres de minadores que se agregaron.

claims.value: Toreno says Moncey acted in chief while intended superior Lannes remained ill at Tudela.
claims.rationale: The preceding lines explain Lannes’s illness at Tudela. Intended authority and physical presence differ. English rendering (ours): "Before formalizing the siege Marshal Moncey, commander-in-chief in Lannes’s absence, intended [the subsequent attack]."

claims.value: Toreno dates Junot’s replacement of Moncey in chief command to 1 January.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "On 1 January General Junot, Duke of Abrantes, replaced Marshal Moncey in chief command."

citations.locator: toreno-t2, printed p. 269, Internet Archive leaf 274; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: El 1.º de enero reemplazó en el mando en gefe al mariscal Moncey el general Junot duque de Abrantes.

claims.value: Toreno dates Lannes’s arrival and assumption of supreme command over the third and fifth corps to 22 January.
claims.rationale: Conflicts with Napoleon’s 11 January statement that Lannes was already before Zaragoza; no replacement clock or reconciliation is invented. English rendering (ours): "Lannes’s arrival on 22 January favoured this intention; recovered from illness, he came to take supreme command of the third and fifth corps."

citations.locator: toreno-t2, printed p. 272, Internet Archive leaf 277; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Favoreció á su intento la llegada el 22 de enero del mariscal Lannes. Restablecido de su indisposicion acudia este á tomar el mando supremo del tercero y quinto cuerpo

claims.value: Napoleon’s 11 January letter says Lannes is before Zaragoza with the fifth and third corps.
claims.rationale: Superior communication differs from Toreno’s 22 January arrival. It might reflect planned/displaced information, but that explanation is not established. English rendering (ours): "You will inform him that Marshal Lannes is before Zaragoza with the fifth and third corps."

claims.value: Toreno places Saint-March second to Palafox, Villalba over artillery, San Genis over engineers and Butrón over cavalry.
claims.rationale: Technical and contingent offices, not automatic outcome credit. English rendering (ours): "Felipe Saint-March was Palafox’s second; General Villalba commanded artillery, Colonel San Genis engineers, and General Butrón 1,400 cavalry."

claims.value: Toreno describes Moncey’s planned attack on Torrero and the troops taking its dominating heights at dawn on 21 December.
claims.rationale: The preceding sentence identifies Moncey’s attack on Torrero. Spanish sorties within a siege do not by themselves recode the principal siege offensive. English rendering (ours): "For that purpose at dawn on the 21st his troops crowned the heights dominating the position."

claims.value: Side B repaired the Aljafería and fortified convents, embankments and a double entrenchment before the second siege.
claims.rationale: Preparation before this siege is treated as inherited to this engagement, not as an inferred battlefield effect of Palafox. English rendering (ours): "On the Ebro’s right bank the Aljafería castle was repaired and improved; convents between it and the Huerva bridge were fortified; a double entrenchment extended to Santa Engracia."

claims.value: Toreno describes stores sufficient to feed 15,000 for six months, plus household and convent provisions.
claims.rationale: Provisioning capacity, not a troop-strength observation, measured ration availability or proof the stocks lasted. English rendering (ours): "Stores held provisions sufficient to feed 15,000 for six months; residents had private household stocks and convents substantial food."

claims.value: Toreno says illness led Palafox to delegate authority to a junta installed during the night of 18–19 February, presided over by Pedro María Ric.
claims.rationale: Late-siege delegated authority, not a permanent appointment registry or a securely fixed replacement boundary. English rendering (ours): "General José de Palafox, struck by the prevailing illness, delegated his powers to a junta installed on the night of 18–19 February; it had 34 members and was presided over by Pedro María Ric."

open_questions: Reconcile opening, reinforcement and capitulation populations and date Moncey/Junot/Lannes and Palafox/Ric authority changes using siege journals and returns.
Deferred: the dated original returns and reports identified above, and any deeper source-lineage reconciliation. No additional research cycle follows merely from this gap.

Source dependence: Bodart is a later compilation. Toreno, Foy, Oman, Saint-Cyr and the official Correspondance are interested or retrospective source families, and embedded/reprinted reports are not extra independent witnesses. Agreement does not establish independence.

A.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Source-specific alternatives below retain their own moment and population. Alternatives/limits: Toreno gives side A 35,000 in the third and fifth corps combined, excluding six artillery, eight sapper and three miner companies. The French letter establishes claimed command presence, not a dated siege return. Bodart’s cumulative engagement convention and Toreno’s initial corps estimate remain separate.
A.command_scope: Printed side-A commander Lannes; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Toreno says Moncey acted in chief while intended superior Lannes remained ill at Tudela. Toreno dates Junot’s replacement of Moncey in chief command to 1 January. Toreno dates Lannes’s arrival and assumption of supreme command over the third and fifth corps to 22 January. Napoleon’s 11 January letter says Lannes is before Zaragoza with the fifth and third corps.
A.army_continuity: Unknown: these passages do not establish a cross-engagement army identity.

B.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Civilians, recruits, regular troops and surrender survivors are not interchangeable. Alternatives/limits: Toreno gives side B an initially expected 14,000–15,000 defenders, rising to 28,000 with fugitives from Tudela; cavalry is separately described at 1,400.
B.command_scope: Printed side-B commander Palafox; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Toreno places Saint-March second to Palafox, Villalba over artillery, San Genis over engineers and Butrón over cavalry. Toreno describes the 18–19 February delegation to Ric’s junta after Palafox fell ill.
B.army_continuity: Unknown: repeated names and formation labels do not establish continuity.
